summary: PR D of the stack-* crates import: adds an `auth` flag to the release gate, a `release-crates` job (stack-auth/stack-profile to crates.io) and `auth-artifacts`/`publish-auth` jobs (seven @cipherstash/auth npm tarballs), all intended to be inert until PR E deletes the @cipherstash/auth entries from FROZEN_PUBLISHERS. Reading the job conditions confirms the new publishing jobs cannot run at head: `release-crates` is gated on `crates-armed`, which reads the still-present @cipherstash/auth entry, and the npm auth jobs need a successful gate that reports auth=true, which a frozen unpublished auth version makes impossible. The one live behaviour change outside the new jobs is the widened push path filter on release-plz.yml: the already-ARMED EQL `release` job (crates.io OIDC, contents: write, GPG key when it decides to publish) now also starts on pushes that touch only the root Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock or the stack-auth/stack-profile crates, which the file's own comment calls a standing credential exposure. Impact if that goes wrong is medium; nothing here can publish an auth or stack-* artefact. Script tests for the new logic exist and the CI job that runs them passed. Advisory: focused review of the release-plz.yml trigger and of the arming coupling that PR E will exercise.

behaviour_changes.description: release-gate.mjs `classify` now returns a third flag, `auth`, for any unpublished name starting with `@cipherstash/auth`, and excludes those names from `js`. `main` writes `auth=` to GITHUB_OUTPUT before evaluating blockers; release.yml's `gate` job exposes it as an output.

release.yml gains `auth-artifacts` (calls the new reusable _build-auth-artifacts.yml) and `publish-auth` (npm OIDC publish of six platform tarballs then the wrapper, then git tags and a GitHub release), both conditioned on production mode and `needs.gate.outputs.auth == 'true'`. The `release` (changeset publish) job now also needs `publish-auth` and requires it to have succeeded whenever auth=true.

release-plz.yml gains `crates-armed` (runs `node scripts/eql-pipeline-armed.mjs crates`) and `release-crates` (release-plz release on the root workspace with contents/pull-requests/id-token write and a GPG import) gated on `armed == 'true'`. The crates switch keys on the npm `@cipherstash/auth` FROZEN_PUBLISHERS entry, so deleting that entry arms crates.io and npm together.

The release-plz.yml push `paths:` filter is widened from packages/eql/** and the workflow file to also include packages/stack-auth/**, packages/stack-profile/**, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, release-plz.toml and cliff.toml. The filter is workflow-level, so it also starts the existing, armed EQL `release` job on those pushes.

New root release-plz.toml (stack-auth and stack-profile in one version_group, all other seven root members release = false); .changeset/config.json gains a fixed group for the seven auth packages; the seven auth package.json files gain repository.directory; lint/caching/supply-chain target lists gain the two new workflows.
New dispatch-only auth-preflight.yml builds all seven tarballs from a supplied ref and smoke-tests the linux-x64-gnu pair; it declares only contents: read and passes no secrets.

failure_scenarios.title: Armed EQL crates.io release job now starts on root-workspace Rust pushes
failure_scenarios.trigger: Any push to main that touches only Cargo.lock / Cargo.toml (e.g. a Dependabot or toolchain bump of the stack-* crates) or packages/stack-auth/** / packages/stack-profile/**.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The new paths sit in the workflow-level `on.push.paths` filter of release-plz.yml (lines 45-54), not on a per-job condition. The EQL `release` job (line 86) is gated only on `eql-armed`, and EQL is armed at head (no @cipherstash/eql entry in FROZEN_PUBLISHERS). So that job, holding id-token: write and contents: write, checks out with persisted credentials, queries crates.io, and imports GPG_PRIVATE_KEY whenever its preflight reads the eql-bindings version as unpublished, including when the crates.io API call fails (line 131).
failure_scenarios.consequence: A credentialed publishing job runs on pushes that release nothing on the EQL line, the standing credential exposure the file's own comment (line 37) set out to avoid. A transient crates.io API failure or a stale EQL state on such a push makes main red with an EQL release error on an unrelated Rust change, and if an eql-bindings version is genuinely unpublished it would publish from a push nobody intended as an EQL release. No auth or stack-* artefact is affected.

missing_verification: A test or job condition asserting the EQL `release` job only runs when packages/eql/** changed (e.g. a dorny/paths-filter or a separate workflow file is not possible for crates.io, so a per-job changed-files check).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Give the EQL `release` job a per-job condition on packages/eql/** having changed (or a cheap changed-files step before any credentialed step), or accept and document the wider trigger in the header comment that currently says the opposite.

failure_scenarios.title: Arming the npm auth line also arms crates.io publishing in one deletion
failure_scenarios.trigger: PR E deletes the @cipherstash/auth FROZEN_PUBLISHERS entries before crates.io Trusted Publishing for stack-auth/stack-profile names cipherstash/stack + release-plz.yml, or before GPG_PRIVATE_KEY exists.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: LINES maps the `crates` line to the npm package `@cipherstash/auth` (eql-pipeline-armed.mjs line 44-52), so `crates-armed` flips with the npm switch. `release-crates` then runs `release-plz release` with workspace `publish = true` on the next matching push.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Not reachable in this PR. At arming time, a missing crates.io publisher entry or secret produces a failing release-plz.yml run on main (loud, nothing published); the coupling is intentional per the PR description but nothing in this repo checks the external prerequisites ahead of time.
